question: What is the primary physiological goal of mechanical ventilation?
explanation: Mechanical ventilation primarily aims to support or replace failing respiratory function to ensure proper oxygenation and carbon dioxide elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h1)

question: Why is mechanical ventilation considered a supportive rather than a curative intervention?

options.A: It assists breathing while the underlying disease is treated
options.B: It permanently alters native lung tissue structure
options.C: It prevents medications from reaching the lower airways
options.D: It completely replaces all metabolic functions of the kidneys

explanation: Ventilators buy time by managing gas exchange while primary medical therapies address the root cause of respiratory failure. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h1)

question: What Glasgow Coma Scale score threshold is widely used to indicate the need for elective airway protection via intubation?
explanation: A Glasgow Coma Scale score of 8 or lower generally indicates a compromised ability to protect the airway, prompting mechanical ventilation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h2)

question: A patient with a severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation is struggling to eliminate carbon dioxide. What category of respiratory failure does this represent?
explanation: An inability to effectively clear carbon dioxide results in elevated arterial carbon dioxide levels, defining hypercapnic respiratory failure. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h2)

question: Which ventilator mode allows the patient to take spontaneous breaths between machine-delivered mandatory breaths?
explanation: SIMV delivers preset mandatory breaths synchronized with patient effort while permitting unassisted spontaneous breaths in between. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h3)

question: Why is Pressure Support Ventilation commonly utilized during the weaning phase?

options.A: It assists spontaneous breaths to help overcome the resistance of the breathing circuit
options.B: It humidifies medical gases before they reach the endotracheal tube
options.C: It completely paralyzes the diaphragm to rest respiratory muscles
options.D: It delivers fixed volume breaths regardless of patient breathing efforts

explanation: Pressure support gives a targeted boost to each spontaneous breath, reducing the work required to pull air through narrow ventilator tubing. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h3)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take when a high-pressure ventilator alarm sounds and the patient shows signs of distress?

options.A: Turn off the ventilator power switch to reset the computer
options.B: Disconnect the patient from the ventilator and bag manually
options.C: Silence the alarm and wait for the respiratory therapist
options.D: Increase the baseline fraction of inspired oxygen immediately

explanation: If ventilator malfunction or severe distress occurs, ensuring immediate ventilation via a manual resuscitation bag takes priority over troubleshooting the machine. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h4)

question: A nurse auscultating the chest of a newly intubated patient hears breath sounds over the right lung but diminished sounds on the left. What complication is most likely occurring?

options.A: Complete displacement of the endotracheal tube into the esophagus
options.B: Severe accumulation of secretions in the left main bronchus
options.C: Accidental mainstem bronchial intubation of the right lung
options.D: Spontaneous tension pneumothorax of the left lung

explanation: Because the right main bronchus is straighter and wider, endotracheal tubes frequently slip into it, resulting in unilateral ventilation of the right side and absent sounds on the left. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h4)

question: How should endotracheal suctioning be scheduled for a mechanically ventilated patient?

options.A: Executed only when family members request it
options.B: Scheduled every two hours around the clock
options.C: Performed strictly on an as-needed basis
options.D: Carried out immediately following every meal

explanation: Routine suctioning causes unnecessary mucosal trauma and hypoxia, so it should only be performed when clinical indicators like secretions or coarse breath sounds are present. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h5)

question: Why is regular application of eye ointment necessary for heavily sedated, mechanically ventilated patients?

options.A: Sedative medications directly increase intraocular fluid production
options.B: Bright lights in intensive care units cause permanent retinal damage
options.C: Loss of the normal blink reflex leads to corneal drying and ulceration
options.D: Systemic dehydration universally affects lacrimal gland function

explanation: Sedatives and neuromuscular blockers inhibit blinking and eyelid closure, leaving corneas exposed to air and vulnerable to severe damage. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h5)

question: At what angle should the head of the bed be maintained to help prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia?
explanation: Elevating the head of the bed significantly reduces the aspiration of gastric and oral secretions into the lower respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of VAP prevention bundles?

options.A: Maintaining head of bed elevation between 30 and 45 degrees
options.B: Daily assessments of readiness to extubate and trial of spontaneous breathing
options.C: Routine changes of the ventilator breathing circuit every 24 hours
options.D: Regular oral care utilizing antiseptic solutions like chlorhexidine

explanation: Current infection control guidelines advise against routine circuit changes every 24 hours, as frequent breaking of the circuit actually increases infection risks. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h6)

question: What type of trial is commonly conducted to assess a patient's readiness to breathe completely on their own?
explanation: A Spontaneous Breathing Trial evaluates whether a patient can sustain adequate breathing and gas exchange without mechanical assistance before extubation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h7)

question: A patient has just been extubated following a successful weaning trial. Which clinical sign requires immediate notification of the medical team?

options.D: Normal heart rate and blood pressure

explanation: Inspiratory stridor indicates laryngeal edema and upper airway narrowing, which can rapidly progress to complete airway obstruction requiring immediate re-intubation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h7)
